# The *"Illumined Divines"* of the Kitáb-i-Íqán: Final Table

In the Kitáb-i-Íqán, Bahá'u'lláh writes that in this Dispensation *"a number of illumined divines, of men of consummate learning, of doctors of mature wisdom, have attained unto His Court,"* and He names some of them ([The Kitáb-i-Íqán](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-iqan_bahaullah/?paraId=para_259&selectionString=kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_9z.0~kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_9z.425)). The same list is quoted in the Báb's *Seven Proofs* ([The Seven Proofs (Dalá'il-i-Sab'ih)](https://bahai-library.com/bab_nicolas_terry_proofs)).

**Source key:** "Íqán notes" = the notes to the Spanish *Libro de Certeza*, which I have translated.

| # | Name in the Íqán | Who he was | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mullá Ḥusayn | The first to believe in the Báb, named by Bahá'u'lláh as **"the recipient of the effulgent glory of the Sun of divine Revelation."** 'Abdu'l-Bahá lists Mullá Ḥusayn of Bushrúyih first among the Báb's disciples who spread through Persia. He led the company that built the fort near Shaykh Ṭabarsí's tomb and fell there. | Íqán ([The Kitáb-i-Íqán](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-iqan_bahaullah/?paraId=para_260&selectionString=kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_a0.0~kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_a0.585)); *A Traveller's Narrative* ([A Traveler’s Narrative](https://oceanlibrary.com/travelers-narrative_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_15&selectionString=abdu-l-baha-traveler-s-narrative-ocean_en_36.0~abdu-l-baha-traveler-s-narrative-ocean_en_36.282)) |
| 2 | Siyyid Yaḥyá (Vaḥíd) | Siyyid Yaḥyáy-i-Dárábí, surnamed Vaḥíd.
| 3 | Mullá Muḥammad-‘Alíy-i-Zanjání | Surnamed Ḥujjat.
| 5 | Mullá Sa‘íd-i-Bárfurúshí | **No account in the library.** Searched in Nabíl, Balyuzi, Momen and Ẓuhúru'l-Ḥaqq: *"Mullá Sa‘íd-i-Bárfurúshí"*, "Mulla Said Barfurushi", "Mulla Said Barfurushiy", Mullá Sa‘íd Bárfurúsh, and Mulla Sa'id-i-Barfurushi with *"Letter of the Living"* and "Babi martyr". No passage describes a Bábí of this name, and the Íqán notes have no entry for him. His name appears only in the Íqán list, quoted again in the Báb's *Seven Proofs*. Similar names in the sources are other men. Shaykh Sa‘íd-i-Hindí was a Letter of the Living sent to India. The *Sa‘ídu'l-‘Ulamá*, the mujtahid of Bárfurúsh, was the Báb's enemy. Quddús was martyred in Bárfurúsh. Nothing shows that any of them is the man in the Íqán. | Íqán list ([The Kitáb-i-Íqán](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-iqan_bahaullah/?paraId=para_260&selectionString=kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_a0.0~kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_a0.585)); *Seven Proofs* ([The Seven Proofs (Dalá'il-i-Sab'ih)](https://bahai-library.com/bab_nicolas_terry_proofs)) |
| 6 | Mullá Ni‘matu'lláh-i-Mázindarání | A Bábí believer martyred at Shaykh Ṭabarsí (my translation of the Íqán note). The library holds no fuller account of him: the Báb's *Seven Proofs* repeats the name within the Íqán list, and Nabíl's list of the Ṭabarsí martyrs has a *"Mullá Ni‘matu'lláh-i-Bárfurúshí"* with no description beside it. He may be the same man, since Bárfurúsh is in Mázindarán, but no passage says so. | Íqán notes ([Libro de Certeza](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_libro_certeza_iqan&chapter=all)); *Seven Proofs* ([The Seven Proofs (Dalá'il-i-Sab'ih)](https://bahai-library.com/bab_nicolas_terry_proofs)); Nabíl's list ([The Dawn-Breakers](https://oceanlibrary.com/dawn-breakers_nabil/?paraId=para_1316&selectionString=dawn-breakers-prod-version_en_139.0~dawn-breakers-prod-version_en_139.31)) |
| 8 | Mullá Mihdíy-i-Khú'í | A close companion of Bahá'u'lláh and tutor to the children of His household, martyred at Ṭabarsí (my translation of the Íqán note). Nabíl also lists a Mullá Maḥmúd-i-Khú'í as a brother of a Mullá Mihdí, but the passage does not say which Mullá Mihdí is meant, so he is not linked to this row. | Íqán notes ([Libro de Certeza](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_libro_certeza_iqan&chapter=all)) |
| 11 | Mullá Báqir | The brother of Mullá Mihdíy-i-Kandí (row 10), martyred at Ṭabarsí. Nabíl records that Bahá'u'lláh attests to the attainments of the two brothers in the Íqán. He is not the Letter of the Living of the same name, who lived to recognise Bahá'u'lláh. | Nabíl, *The Dawn-Breakers*, Ṭabarsí martyr no. 153 ([shoghi-effendi-trans-011-the-dawn-breakers_en](https://oceanoflights.org/shoghi-effendi-trans-011-the-dawn-breakers-en/#:~:text=153.%20Mull%C3%A1%20B%C3%A1qir%2C%20brother%20of%20Mull%C3%A1%20Mihd%C3%AD%2C%20both,testifies%20in%20the%20Kitab-i-Iqan)); Íqán notes ([Libro de Certeza](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_libro_certeza_iqan&chapter=all)) |
| 12 | Mullá ‘Abdu'l-Khálíq-i-Yazdí | First a Jewish priest, then a convert to Islám and the Shaykhí school, and converted to the Bábí Faith by Mullá Ḥusayn. | Íqán notes ([Libro de Certeza](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_libro_certeza_iqan&chapter=all)) |
| 13 | Mullá ‘Alíy-i-Baraqání | An uncle of Ṭáhirih and one of the most learned and famous Shaykhís. After becoming a Bábí he was one of the most active and capable Bábí expositors in Tihrán. | Íqán notes ([Libro de Certeza](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_libro_certeza_iqan&chapter=all)) |

Bahá'u'lláh adds *"and others, well nigh four hundred in number, whose names are all inscribed upon the 'Guarded Tablet' of God." ([The Kitáb-i-Íqán, #248](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-iqan_bahaullah/?paraId=para_260&selectionString=kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_a0.0~kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_a0.585))* ([The Seven Proofs (Dalá'il-i-Sab'ih)](https://bahai-library.com/bab_nicolas_terry_proofs))

**Open points**
- Row 5, Mullá Sa‘íd-i-Bárfurúshí: the library has no account of him under any of the spellings searched.
- Row 6 may be the same man as the Ni‘matu'lláh of Bárfurúsh in Nabíl's martyr list, but no passage confirms it.
- Row 8 rests on the Íqán notes alone, and no passage links him to the Khú'í brothers in Nabíl.
